answer: In PoA, identity verification requires a prescribed chain of modular squarings, where each output is the input to the next, and a Wesolowski proof verifies the completed delay efficiently. GPUs can duplicate hardware, but cannot parallelize this dependency chain across devices or reduce its sequential depth; every simulated clone therefore requires an independent timed computation. From terrace to tide to vertex, this physical bottleneck makes Sybil expansion costly and time-bound.
